content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To wake up for school, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Step out of the shower (1 minute)
Step 2. Put on a fresh pair of socks (30 seconds)
Step 3. Check the weather forecast on your phone (2 minutes)
Step 4. Pack a notebook into your backpack (10 seconds)
Step 5. Grind coffee beans (1 minute)
Step 6. Apply deodorant (20 seconds)
Step 7. Step into the shower and lather up (8 minutes)
Step 8. Comb and style your hair (4 minutes)
Step 9. Turn off the alarm clock (5 seconds)
Step 10. Zip up the main compartment of your bag (5 seconds)
Step 11. Put on your left shoe (15 seconds)
Step 12. Tie your shoelaces (30 seconds)
Step 13. Pour water into the coffee maker (30 seconds)
Step 14. Place your backpack by the front door (20 seconds)
Step 15. Locate your clean shoes in the closet (1 minute)
Step 16. Decide whether to bring an umbrella (30 seconds)
Step 17. Dry yourself off with a towel (3 minutes)
Step 18. Put on your underwear (45 seconds)
Step 19. Open your eyes and stretch (2 minutes)
Step 20. Grab your school ID from the nightstand (10 seconds)
Step 21. Sit up on the edge of the bed (1 minute)
Step 22. Pull on your trousers (1 minute)
Step 23. Put on your school shirt (2 minutes)
Step 24. Slide your feet into your shoes (15 seconds)
Step 25. Check that you have your pens (30 seconds)
Step 26. Fasten your belt (20 seconds)
Step 27. Put on your right shoe (15 seconds)
Step 28. Pick up your phone and ID (20 seconds)
Step 29. Rinse the soap off your body (2 minutes)
Step 30. Adjust the shower water temperature (45 seconds)

These ordering constraints need to be obeyed when executing above steps:
Step 1 must precede Step 29.
Step 2 must precede Step 22.
Step 3 must precede Step 16.
Step 3 must precede Step 30.
Step 4 must precede Step 14.
Step 5 must precede Step 13.
Step 6 must precede Step 23.
Step 7 must precede Step 1.
Step 8 must precede Step 27.
Step 9 must precede Step 3.
Step 9 must precede Step 13.
Step 9 must precede Step 15.
Step 10 must precede Step 14.
Step 11 must precede Step 27.
Step 13 must precede Step 7.
Step 13 must precede Step 17.
Step 15 must precede Step 11.
Step 17 must precede Step 18.
Step 18 must precede Step 23.
Step 19 must precede Step 3.
Step 19 must precede Step 10.
Step 19 must precede Step 28.
Step 20 must precede Step 28.
Step 21 must precede Step 2.
Step 21 must precede Step 13.
Step 22 must precede Step 23.
Step 22 must precede Step 26.
Step 22 must precede Step 27.
Step 24 must precede Step 12.
Step 25 must precede Step 14.
Step 25 must precede Step 26.
Step 28 must precede Step 24.
Step 29 must precede Step 17.
Step 29 must precede Step 18.
Step 30 must precede Step 1.

Question: Assume that you need to execute all the steps to complete the task and that infinite resources are available. What is the shortest possible time to wake up for school?

The problem contains exactly 30 numbered steps. Your action ids must be:
step1, step2, step3, step4, step5, step6, step7, step8, step9, step10, step11, step12, step13, step14, step15, step16, step17, step18, step19, step20, step21, step22, step23, step24, step25, step26, step27, step28, step29, step30

Return only the JSON object.
